{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/trial.csv')

# Check for duplicates in patient_id
patient_id_counts = df['patient_id'].value_counts()
duplicate_patients = patient_id_counts[patient_id_counts > 1]

# Report number of unique patients and re-tested patients
n_unique_patients = len(df['patient_id'].unique())
n_retested = len(duplicate_patients)

print(f'Unique patient_ids: {n_unique_patients}')
print(f'Re-tested patients (appear >1 time): {n_retested}')

# Check if there are any control-arm patients with moderate severity
control_moderate = df[(df['arm'] == 'control') & (df['severity'] == 'moderate')]
has_control_moderate = len(control_moderate) > 0

print(f'Control arm, moderate severity patients exist: {has_control_moderate}')

# Check responded is binary
responded_unique = df['responded'].unique()
print(f'Unique values in responded: {responded_unique}')

# Check if assay_batch or biomarker_baseline affect responded
# We're not using biomarker_baseline or assay_batch for this analysis, but just to confirm
# that they don't interfere with the 'responded' variable

# Summary: check for -999 in biomarker_baseline
n_neg999 = (df['biomarker_baseline'] == -999).sum()
print(f'Number of -999 in biomarker_baseline: {n_neg999}')

# Return results
{'n_unique_patients': n_unique_patients, 'n_retested': n_retested, 'has_control_moderate': has_control_moderate, 'responded_unique': responded_unique, 'n_neg999': n_neg999}"}
